# Why does fixing some packets to reduce remote operation delay lead to continuous jitter?

> **Current answer:** When the average production rate is below 250 Hz, the queue becomes full; if the full queue is interpreted as no target, zero value, or sudden retention, the joint targets are discontinuous. A more reliable approach is to resample at the target timestamp, interpolate within a bounded delay, and use last safe values, speed limits, or damping degradation for underload, while monitoring underrun.

## Key terms

- Queue underrun (buffer underrun) (队列欠载)
- Timestamp resampling (时间戳重采样)
- Safe hold (安全保持)

## Problem and symptoms

- How can 50 Hz upper commands be stably sent to the 250 Hz lower execution loop?
- Why do queue overflow and queue underflow both manifest as robot jitter?
- Discard new packets after queue overflow, leading to long delays and sudden large oscillations.
- Delay reduces after discarding 1/5 packets, but the queue becomes full and continues to jitter.

## Environment

- Upper remote operation: 50 Hz/20 ms; lower C++ execution: 250 Hz/4 ms; ROS topic; maximum queue: 5000, cumulative queue after 10 packets: executed.

## Priority diagnostics

- Record the upper production timestamp, lower consumption timestamp, queue depth, packet loss count, and target continuity continuity.

## Possible causes

- Inconsistent clock/scheduling between Python and C++.
- Fixed five-part interpolation does not handle network jitter and production/consumption offset.

## Attempts

- Divide each 20 ms command into 5 parts for 4 ms execution.
- Discard 1/5 of the packets to reduce queue growth.
- Plan to switch the Python middle layer to C++.

## Result

- First scheme still causes queue overflow; second scheme reduces delay but causes underload jitter; final C++ rewrite direction is not publicly available or reproducible.

## Limitations

- Raises questions about the factual basis of the article; no public timestamp curve, packet loss rate, or final rewrite result has been provided.

## Safety notes

- Limit joint speed, position increments, and torque before real machine testing; during queue anomalies, maintain last safe target or enter damping mode; do not directly convert missing frames into abrupt changes.

## Image and visual evidence

- The Mermaid diagram in the text explains the structure of upper asynchronous write to the queue and lower strict periodic read from the queue; the diagram is conceptual and not real-time sequence evidence.

## Applicability boundary

- Applies to remote operation chains where the upper sampling rate is lower than the lower control rate.
